text: convert, five jobs, two designs: the Caruca paper's v1 and the agent in run 8
purple = done by a language model · blue = done by hand-written code · red text = where the two differ most. Section numbers refer to the Caruca paper (arXiv:2510.14279).

v1, as the
paper designs it

a fixed pipeline:
one model step,
then code
1 Syntax: a model writes it

GPT-4o reads a bundled copy of
the manual (not -help, not the
binary), with worked examples
for touch, rm, mv and ls; told
not to add what the manual
lacks; up to 3 tries (section 3)
2 Choose what to run: code

every combination of up to N
flags with typed values; input
files from a fixed set that
includes a JPEG image
(section 4)
3 Run and observe: code

each case in a throwaway
file-system layer (OverlayFS),
fresh namespace, chroot;
strace records every file
read and write (section 5)
4 Decide behaviour: rules

inputs and outputs from the
recorded reads and writes;
stateless only if split runs
join to one run's output
(section 6.3)
5 Write per consumer: code

adapters translate one
internal result into PaSh and
Shseer JSON, POSH YAML and
ShellCheck Haskell
(section 6.4)

v1's grammars hold the manual's
248 names, its typo
-connected-component, no '+'
forms, -view as a flag; the agent:
522 spellings tried on the binary

v1 generates 7,308 command lines
at 1 flag, 917,154 at 2; the
agent ran about 6,800 in all

the paper projects 98.72 hours
for 2 flags, its one outlier
(section 7.4); the agent: 21.5
min, one plain /tmp folder

v1's first annotation (2024-11):
'found no successful runs,
defaulting to side-effectful';
the agent: reasoned rules

v1's committed annotation has
had no cases since 2024-12;
the agent: all three PaSh files
(not yet loaded in PaSh)
one Claude Code session, claude-fable-5-1 at medium effort: every step below is the model's own choice, in 33 tool calls and $6.04

run 8:
the agent

no pipeline:
one model does
every job
1 Syntax: model + binary
2 Choose what to run: model

loops over every name, '-' and
'+', with 0 to 3 extra words;
one option at a time (a few
checks pair two); ~3,700
runs before writing
3 Run and observe: model

plain /tmp/cvt; stdin from
/dev/null and a 5 s timeout
(after one hang); reads error
text and whether out.png
appears; no strace, no container
4 Decide behaviour: model

all operands but the last are
read, the last is written;
'-', 'fmt:-', -identify, -write
use standard streams; not
splittable (no probe)
5 Write PaSh's form: model

a script writes the table and
the syntax; own harness tests
them 3 times; report says 522
passed (509 tested, 1 still
flagged)

Scale for convert. The paper names it as the one command that does not finish within a day even at two flags, and says its behaviour is simple: read one file, write another.
The agent spent its effort on the interface instead (which words are options, how many words each consumes), testing one option at a time; only a few checks paired two.

v1 is shown as the paper designs it (sections 2-7); v1's counts are from 'caruca generate convert --number' on the Mac, its annotation history from v1's git log. Method, not quality, is compared here.
